# Core LEGO architecture

**Canonical for:** the current core domains, the strangler boundary and the nesting rule.

The repository declares **26 core LEGO domains**. That number is
generated from `manifest/domains.json` on every build — if a document elsewhere
states a different count, that document is stale and this one is right.

## What a LEGO must declare

Every domain declares one responsibility boundary, one owner, a public contract
and a contract version, plus capabilities, operations, permissions, interaction
classes, dependencies, forbidden dependencies, lifecycle, availability,
criticality, trust, transport, degradation, migration state, replacement
strategy, resource profile, tests and evidence.

A LEGO may be replaced internally without forcing consumers to rewrite. **The
contract is the seam** — that is the entire point of the decomposition.

## Kinds of thing

The vocabulary below is kept distinct on purpose. Most architectural confusion
in this project has come from collapsing two of these into one word.

| Kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `lego` | A unit of ownership with its own contract, lifecycle, data and tests. |
| `sub-lego` | A nested unit inside a LEGO. Reaching it requires an explicit declaration naming the child; nesting grants nothing. |
| `contract` | The stable public surface. Lives above JS/Rust/WASM. |
| `provider` | Where an implementation is sourced from. |
| `adapter` | A translator at an edge between an external protocol and an internal contract. |
| `runtime` | Where an agent or system executes. |
| `capability` | An abstraction of WHAT can be done, independent of how. |
| `operation` | One named, permissioned, interaction-classed action on a capability. |
| `ui-experience` | A product surface rendered by the frontend. Not a LEGO. |
| `artifact` | A referenced result. Never inlined into an event. |
| `event` | A small, bounded record of something that happened. |
| `implementation` | The swappable realisation of a contract. |

## Strangler boundary

The legacy REST aggregate is a temporary boundary, not the future architecture:

```
legacy REST -> compatibility boundary -> target LEGO contract -> target LEGO implementation
```

Each carve-out picks one route family, gives the contract to the target domain,
publishes and locks it, mounts the new surface ahead of legacy routing, deletes
the legacy handler, and lets the architecture gate verify that the aggregate
actually shrank.

- Never create a "misc" domain to make ownership look complete.
- Never add new business logic to legacy.
- The legacy aggregate must shrink over time, and a gate must be able to see it.

## Nesting

- A sub-LEGO is a full registry entry with `parent` set to its parent's id. It declares its own owner, contract version, dependencies, capabilities and tests.
- Nest only where the split is justified by a real boundary. Depth is capped at 3 (parent -> child -> grandchild) to prevent decorative hierarchies.
- A sub-LEGO's paths must live inside its parent's paths — a child cannot own code outside its parent.
- A sub-LEGO inherits nothing implicitly: dependencies and forbidden directions are declared per entry.
- A parent may reach its own children's public contracts without declaring a dependency (composition inside one domain); reaching a child's internals is still forbidden.
- An outside consumer may depend on a sub-LEGO's public contract only if it declares that sub-LEGO in dependsOn. Sibling-internal reach (A.sub -> B.sub internal) is always forbidden.
- A sub-LEGO may be owned by a different agent than its parent; ownership remains single-writer at every level.

Maximum depth: **3**.

## Surface aliases

A surface alias maps an external/UI vocabulary word to ONE canonical capability-owning domain. It creates no capability, no contract and no ownership. If two words mean genuinely different things they must be different capabilities, not aliases.

| Surface word | Canonical domain | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executions` | `execution` |  |
| `workflows` | `workflow` |  |
| `credentials` | `credentials` |  |
| `projects` | `workspace` |  |
| `node-types` | `node-registry` |  |

> An alias creates no capability, no contract and no ownership. Ownership never
> resolves through an alias.
